Somarendra Nath Biswas, DAG, instructed by Haridas Paul, Advocate-on-Record ------- For the petitioners 
Raziuddin Ahmed, Advocate instructed by Ms. Shanahara Begum Advocate-on-Record. --------- For the respondents

Vs.

full_judgment: Here, in this case, the High Court Davison in fact, passed the impugned order to compel the executive to pay government petition of salaries inasmuch as the government did decided as yet to pay salaries to them or even did not assure them that the Government did decide as yet to pay salaries to them or even did not assure them that the Government would pay the same. In absence of the statutory obligation, the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constantine is not justified in issuing mandamus for payment of salary since a mandamus cannot lie in the absence of a legal right based on the existence of statutory duty. The mere fact that recognition ad registration have been granted to an institutions or, for that matter, for conducting new course of subject would not give rise to a presumption of a financial sanction. A financial liability cannot be imposed on the Government to reimburse the salary payable to the teachers and staffs of the private college on the basis of such presumption. No mandamus can be issued for payment of salary by the government in the absence of the prior sanction of the Government.
